interactions.title: The gate statue welcomes expected guests
lines: DM: So as you begin to fly up, one of the statues speaks in a booming voice, "Travelers, stop and introduce yourselves to the great King Brimskarda," and repeats in like 9 different languages. So it is literally—it's an animated statue. It's—yeah.
DM: I get the picture. The the statue says, "Welcome, guests. You are expected. Please proceed."

before: DM: He seemed to think Vindristjarna could fit through the gate. Why don't we just fly through the gate?
Seeker: Okay, we'll take it very slow.
Delwath: But, like—you begin— is this picture accurate? Does not—actually, it's not into a building. Right? It's just a gate.
Seeker: Yeah, this picture's pretty accurate in—into a big open—
DM: Into a big— It doesn't have the glacier courtyard, but beyond the gate there's like a big giant caldera carved out of ice. It doesn't go into a building.
after: Seeker: So we inch forward through the gate. Don't want to scrape anything up.
DM: There's, there's like 10 foot clearing, roughly, like 5 feet on either side. It's like maybe 90, a hundred feet wide. So it's a bit of a tight squeeze. But actually—
Seeker: Because I can see out from the surfaces of the ship, I'm well suited for this type of specific—
DM: To navigate.
Seeker: Especially taking this slow.

interactions.title: Gifts, stories, and hospitality at Brimskarda’s court
lines: DM: And he like sort of waves, says in this booming voice, in Common as, as you approach: "Greetings. Welcome to my home of Isenborg! It is a pleasure to see travelers such as yourself come to honor this court. Please come, tell me of yourself," and he like motions. Yep.
DM: A sort of air of friendly superiority.

Delwath: And I'll start by presenting this giant baked meat, shaped into an elk slash dragon thing, and I think we should give them— I think this Horn would be a good gift. We can. We can afford the 400 to 600 gold.

Delwath: So I was gonna have the horn around its neck, right? And present this and and like, tell them we have come bearing, and obviously [garbled], with my guy. ((Gift mechanics))"We've come. We are travelers. We are heading east. We have come to seek his advice on the dangers of the land, and hear his stories and pay our respects."
DM: He kind of smiles and and claps his hands, and "Did not realize such civilized folk came in such small packages."
DM: And he sort of motions for you to set your gifts—yeah, on—in front of him. Yeah. Yeah. And he like claps his his hands. And—

DM: Coming out from the the side hall is—you see another frost giant. ... She is somewhat older and she kind of walks with her head down a little bit, and you can see one of her arms like is injured somehow. It must have like been broken and not healed properly, or something, cause it like doesn't move quite right.

DM: And, and he, he sort of yells over to her in giant which Delwath understands: "Vetrdis! Move that quickly. Now take this nice present and make it the centerpiece of our feast. Hurry! We have guests, you—" Says some word, in Giant that you interpret to be some kind of like derogatory term. And, and she kind of walks over a little bit, and then like clumsily picks up this these things and and begins to founder walk off.

DM: And he then turns to you and says in Common, "Now, please tell me your stories. I would love to hear your travels and tales. We get so few visitors of quality in this place. I hear tell that you too have killed one dragon. Is that correct?" Just not 1, 3 like me, but—
Delwath: We—we have killed one dragon.
DM: That is no small feat for somebody so little.

Delwath: A daemon quite fearsome. I mean, what's—what was the demon's name? But M— Something the Corruptor. Mashtu, Mashtu the Corruptor a— I—now, I can't even remember what the demon was—like the size of a small pond. Yeah, he is pretty big, 20 feet, right? Like, you know, I'll describe Mashtu a bit right? And of course—
Delwath: The Undying, perhaps our most dangerous opponent we have faced: Grash, the undying possessing of a ring prevents death.
DM: "Troublesome magic. Good of you to stamp that out. I appreciate your service."

DM: Like halfway through he reaches beside the throne. He picks up a barrel and just takes a swig from it of like a giant barrel of, of beer, and he sort of looks around at you. "Where are my manners?" And he shouts, "Vetrdis, Vetrdis," in Giant. "Get some puny little things for them to drink out of. Take some of the dwarf stuff, they won't notice. Well, it doesn't matter if they notice." Few minutes later.

Delwath: And then, as the story sort of winds down I'll explain that we are heading east, and we heard that he was the master of these parts, and we do not feel it would be right to pass by without paying our respects, and asking if there was any advice he would pass on to us of the dangers we might face further east, or how he would navigate them.

DM: ((Room inspection))So as you're talking as Seeker's looking around, the the woman Vetrdis comes back and she's bringing— she is carrying like a tray that has another barrel of what looks like beer. And then 5 glass—5 like little glasses like normal human size. Actually, relatively like, like pint glasses, basically. But they look super tiny, even as she who is not as tall or as big as the king, brings them over and and puts them down. And she's also brought on this cushions like sort of relatively large pillow, like sofa cushion size pillows and she sort of bows, and and says in giant to the king, "My lord, I brought as you asked, and I thought maybe your guests might be cold sitting on the ice. I hope it's okay."

DM: And he kind of smiles and he motions. "Please sit. Food will be here soon. Drink. I will tell you my tales of glory, my battles against the dangers in the East, and you will learn what to do if you wish to survive in this horrible territory." And he motions and like, she makes this sort of awkward— yeah—attempt to pour from this barrel into these tiny little glasses kind of spills things, and he yells at her a bit, and she starts off.
Delwath: When she starts to try to pour, I'm gonna cast shape water and just direct it into each glass.

before: Seeker: Oh, nice, Mike.
DM: Exceedingly cold. Like, I mean, you are—this is 15, 20 degrees colder than outside, at least, like you're basically stepping into a freezer.

DM: Everything is may—like, carved of ice like these massive pillars of ice that stretch up 50 feet into the sky. And there's just a huge cavernous space. And you can see sitting on the throne—I have to move Eric and Kong—sitting on the throne. Although there's no giant on this throne, because DALL-E is not quite that good yet. Is this frost giant. He has a white—the longish white beard wearing armor. There's a giant axe resting against the side of the of the throne.

DM: His—his hair is pulled back, and he's got a circlet like a silver circlet set with blue stones, probably sapphires or something, tying back his hair, which is also like tied in a ponytail in the back. He has bluish eyes. The light is sort of casting a pale blue glow over everything which makes this— his skin look almost have a bluish tint.

DM: Although, his hair is white, he definitely does not look old. This is a man in his prime, although it's hard to tell exactly how old the Frost Giant is. They live like hundreds of years. So it's hard to say, and he—he smiles and stands up as you all approach, and he kind of looks, looks down at you in this kind of smiling— you know, it's not— It's not exactly a welcoming smile. It's more of a you know, "These are— This is great to have something new in my court" smile.
after: Kenzo: Okay, as I'm also like— starts dozing because it reminds him of like when he was an acolyte monk, and like the the kind of main monks were like telling you like, "What's gonna be on the test." And this—they're like, this is exactly what's gonna happen instead of getting really tired, because just reminds him of like, you know, what's—you know? You pay attention for this part, and then it's gonna happen. And so you start like subconsciously dozing.

DM: So he begins to tell stories, and it's clear that Brimskarda can talk at length about his heroics. He speaks about fighting dragons, about the you know, the his first— his first battle, his first dragon, that his first battle that he fought when he was a young king against the White Dragon, Grimwinter, who he crushed, freeing the people of the Svinjo— he doesn't— He actually doesn't call them— the Svinjo Mountains, he calls them— He calls them Hrimthur—freeing the people of Hrimthur from Grimwinter's reign of terror.

DM: It was a turning point. He talks about like everybody was so grateful and happy to be freed from the dragon's reign. The tribute came for years. Blah, blah, blah. It goes on at length, basically about how amazing he was to kill this dragon.

DM: Talks about iceworms. Describes his fights against them, says, "The real thing you gotta watch out for is when they swallow you," and he looks at you, and he says, "Never been a problem for me, but—" Points at you.
Seeker: What happens when they swallow you?

interactions.title: Brimskarda’s tales of iceworms and dragons
lines: DM: So he begins to tell stories, and it's clear that Brimskarda can talk at length about his heroics. He speaks about fighting dragons, about the you know, the his first— his first battle, his first dragon, that his first battle that he fought when he was a young king against the White Dragon, Grimwinter, who he crushed, freeing the people of the Svinjo— he doesn't— He actually doesn't call them— the Svinjo Mountains, he calls them— He calls them Hrimthur—freeing the people of Hrimthur from Grimwinter's reign of terror.

DM: It was a turning point. He talks about like everybody was so grateful and happy to be freed from the dragon's reign. The tribute came for years. Blah, blah, blah. It goes on at length, basically about how amazing he was to kill this dragon.

DM: Talks about iceworms. Describes his fights against them, says, "The real thing you gotta watch out for is when they swallow you," and he looks at you, and he says, "Never been a problem for me, but—" Points at you.
Seeker: What happens when they swallow you?
DM: He looks—he looks kind of puzzled, like, squints down. He picks up the barrel and chugs some beer. "Food. You know the concept of food? I'm saying you are its food."
Seeker: So that's, that's a situation to avoid. That's your recommendation?
DM: "Maybe some people like getting eaten. Who am I to judge? But yes, I would avoid that thing, that situation," and he was—
Seeker: Did they—? What vulnerabilities of this fearsome creature do you cleverly exploit in order to defeat it? Is there a way to surprise it, or a way to strike it that especially harms it?

DM: Wow! Let me tell you the tale of my fight against the ice worm. One—first thing you must know is how to spot them. They go—they bury in the permafrost. But the trees will sway as they move. If you see trees swaying in a line, you know where to set your ambush. That is the first thing you have to watch for.

DM: So I'm trying to look up that—here we go. When they spot you they will erupt, opening a giant fissure in the earth. Well, I say, giant— not such a giant for a giant for you, about my size. Do not fall into it. That will be very bad for you. And then watch out for its tongues: lash out, wrap around you, and drag you into its gaping maw. If you're swallowed, your only hope is to stab its stomach as quickly as you can before the stomach acid consumes you.
DM: Vulnerabilities? Well, the best you can do—one of those tongues lashes out at you, hit the tongue as fast as you can. An axe is good.

DM: Strike it and make it pull back before it can pull you into its mouth. I had 3 tongues wrapped around me, all 3 of its tongues. With one mighty blow of my axe I cut through all of them. Watched it rear up in the sky, aimed my blow and struck its neck. I don't think you could do that, but maybe a similar strategy adapted for smaller creatures could work.
Delwath: I have 2 sort of questions I want to be asking as he's talking about these things.
Delwath: The first is, when he was talking about the dragon, any idea of when this was would be useful. But he said, "He's a young king," right? Like, so—
DM: When this was— about 60 years ago.

Delwath: And then the other question is, as he's talking about these—killing these monsters, does he ever do anything with the carcasses? Does he sell it? We've heard rumors that these people that there's people who buy these things. Is that true?
DM: He kind of looks— so, at— "Why would I—why would I resort to base commerce when my loyal subjects bring everything I need to me to honor my great might in battle?"

DM: "Those—there's the little people of the wood run around, and they scavenge things. They have nothing better to do than try to sneak around and scavenge at the bits and pieces that are left from our kills. But I let them. What difference does it make? But sell? Huh! I never would need to sell anything for small folk to deal with."
DM: The the wizards will apparently buy anything for those who are desperate.

DM: I've heard some of the the little folk of the woods survive by— since they are not worth the effort to protect. I mean, what could they do for me? Why would I protect them? Some of them trade with the wizards, some of them, even, I believe, are protected by the wizards.
DM: But it took—last winter, it took 9 of those wizards to kill one dragon. I could have killed it by myself. I don't give them much thought.
Seeker: Dragon killing. How many of these white dragons are there? Do many remain?
DM: You're going east and you don't know about the dragon spawn of Vimfrost?
Riswynn: We did stop to ask.

DM: It's a good thing that you came to my kingdom, for you surely would have died without my advice. Some hundreds of years ago great Dragon Vimfrost ruled the lands before my time. I think if I had been born in those days he would not have established such a presence. There's an option.

DM: Vimfrost lived far to the east. The base of his territory was far to the east. In— He lived beyond the river that the—that the humans call yeah, the Ket, in the Yokolscar Mountains, covered in glaciers, buried in snow.
DM: Vimfrost was— the rumors are that he was one of the most powerful of his kind, and hundreds of young dragons were spawned from him. Perhaps a thousand.
DM: Yes. And they have raided the Southern lands ever since Vimfrost was killed.
DM: Oh, nobody important— a human king, I think. Derik somebody. It was all politics.
Delwath: He must have had many, many—months war— He must have had many, many, many helpers to achieve what you would have done by yourself.

DM: Oh, yes, and, and of course he had many helpers. Even some giants. Bjarnfrost fought in the—in Vimfrost's war; he never came back. They call him Bjarnfrost the Mighty, but I do not think he was that mighty if he could not come back from a silly little war with humans.
DM: But that was hundreds of years ago. Isenborg was a different place then. Different time. Doesn't— It's not really relevant to my rule.
DM: So yes, many dragons, Vimfrost spawn, and many of them, I believe we're— fought each other for dominance and power, and have come south in waves ever since. But my people are safe.
Seeker: Have the dragons ever attacked this stronghold?
DM: Oh, yes, Grimwinter tried right after I claimed the throne. Foolish choice of that pathetic beast.
Seeker: Okay. I wouldn't get too close to the giant's face.

DM: Yeah, he's sort of looking down at you. He is still talking about, about white dragons. "After I killed Grimwinter, there was Eskanyar. I had to go find his lair. I smashed that ice cave like it was nothing." Keeps going, still talking.

before: DM: But yeah, that seems to be— And then you can see that there's like in the back past the throne, there's like a—there's like the big one side there's like a big door that leads off somewhere, and the other side there's a very little door like 6 feet tall.

DM: That probably leads to some service entrance or service quarters. So as you're talking as Seeker's looking around, the the woman Vetrdis comes back and she's bringing— she is carrying like a tray that has another barrel of what looks like beer. And then 5 glass—5 like little glasses like normal human size. Actually, relatively like, like pint glasses, basically. But they look super tiny, even as she who is not as tall or as big as the king, brings them over and and puts them down. And she's also brought on this cushions like sort of relatively large pillow, like sofa cushion size pillows and she sort of bows, and and says in giant to the king, "My lord, I brought as you asked, and I thought maybe your guests might be cold sitting on the ice. I hope it's okay."

DM: And he kind of smiles and he motions. "Please sit. Food will be here soon. Drink. I will tell you my tales of glory, my battles against the dangers in the East, and you will learn what to do if you wish to survive in this horrible territory." And he motions and like, she makes this sort of awkward— yeah—attempt to pour from this barrel into these tiny little glasses kind of spills things, and he yells at her a bit, and she starts off.
Delwath: When she starts to try to pour, I'm gonna cast shape water and just direct it into each glass.

Kenzo: Okay, as I'm also like— starts dozing because it reminds him of like when he was an acolyte monk, and like the the kind of main monks were like telling you like, "What's gonna be on the test." And this—they're like, this is exactly what's gonna happen instead of getting really tired, because just reminds him of like, you know, what's—you know? You pay attention for this part, and then it's gonna happen. And so you start like subconsciously dozing.
after: Seeker: Hmm.

DM: At this point, as he's like halfway into the story of how he killed Eskanyar, the, the woman Vetrdis comes back with like a trail of 5 or 6— I'd say, 6 stoneborn—2 stoneborn and 4 dwarven servants who are kind of following her, and she is carrying what looks like—I— like a whole roast goat, like one of these massive 10 foot long goats on a giant platter, and then sort of next to it, the, the goat's been sort of moved around a little bit, so it's like curled around this very small, but still in, you know, giant, but also small compared to the goat centerpiece that Delwath made.

DM: And, and then it's like piled with these sort of weird kind of—they almost look like like blue-white melons, like frozen— if you took like a cantaloupe and turned it bluish, and then froze it solid and with, like, there's like cracks running down the top.

DM: And she puts this stuff down and clears, clears the space. There's like steps leading up to the up to the, the giants’ throne, and she puts this down. She, like, begins to set down the this giant platter that she's carrying, and there's like folding legs on the bottom of this tray that she unfolds to make it into a table. And so it's kind of in the center of the hall. And it stands maybe 10 feet tall.
Seeker: Family.

interactions.title: The succession of Kaldhalla and the unwanted historian
lines: DM: So over the course of the evening, as you feast and eat and talk you do hear—so, so you do hear the story of how Brimskarda came to power sometime after—so apparently this war with Vimfrost kind of— a number of giants died in this war with Vimfrost, including Bjarnfrost, the Mighty, the old, the old King of, of of— is—in Isenborg. Right? Isenborg is the name of the steading. The hall is the palace. The—
Delwath: There's a big time gap between when the old King died and yeah.

DM: So many of the frost giants after Vimfrost's war, ended up backing Cha'mutte and fought in Cha'mutte's armies, and they were led by a woman, Freyvidra, who ruled, but was allied with the dragons, and would not fight against the dragons. And the way Brimskarda tells it, she was like— She was like a servant of the children of Vim—of Vimfrost. She would raid the stoneborn and the dwarves, and the the little people of the forest, the Vargald, and rather than keeping the tribute, she would leave it for the dragons.

DM: And there was a faction that got sick of her weakness, her incompetence, her inability to protect the giants, the impoverishment of the kingdom of Kaldhalla, which is what he calls the entire Frost Giant kingdom. And so they killed her, and then Brimskarda fought off the dragons and claimed the throne. And since then has restored the rightful order of the North, where tribute flows to the frost giants, not the dragons.

DM: And that was like 60 years. So, the— what was the other question? Anybody who— So you get the sense that you are currently feasting with— So as the feast goes on, it's obvious that this is like Brimskarda's family. Basically, it's you know, his wife, his sister, his brother-in-law, his nephews. These are—this is like the core of the of the court of Isenborg. None of these people are going to leave court on a you know, on, on a quest with you.

DM: There are other giants. If you want to spend the night and sort of ask around, there's like at least another 6 giants that live here. That would certainly be a possibility. But you're not going to convince any of—

Delwath: Well, right? But presumably these people know the other 6 giants. Right? Yeah, yeah, like, it's not so much about Con— It's not like we're trying to convince one of these 6 people to come with us. It's more we're just trying to find out, are there any giants who live here, who are crazy adventure wanderers who might be interested.
Wellby: Or even just have the knowledge and can, like—or just—
Riswynn: Like I said, somebody who's gone East for their own reasons.
DM: Okay. Hmm. So you, you get— you just say, "No, nobody's interested"—multiple possibilities here.

DM: So basically, your understanding from from like listening to the conversations, and just like being curious and friendly and open, and sort of flattering of of Brimskarda, is that you know, he's got his family, and then his like loyalists, right? The the guys who are sort of hanging around the palace. And then there's a handful of tribute collectors. And, and basically there's sort of 2 possibilities for somebody who might be could—who could be convinced to travel.

DM: One would be one of the tribute collectors, like the people who goes around taking stuff from the dwarves and the stoneborn, who's widely traveled, who's been out east, would probably ask for payment. I mean, he— You could hire one of these people as a guide for some decent fee. There's some question as to whether there's— how they would get home.

DM: But it could be all be negotiated, right? There's definitely people who have traveled out into the East. They don't really bother collecting tribute from the Vargald, because they're not under Brimskarda's protection, and they don't make anything useful according to the king. And it's not like they have treasure that's worth taking. They kind of just let the dragons kill them if the dragons come and— dragons need to—they—dragons need some release valve right? Like, you can't completely stop dragons from rampaging. So you know, every now and then one will come out, and if they kill some of the Vargald doesn't really matter to them. But they do travel out into the forest sometimes.

DM: The other possibility would be the good for nothing, son of the of it—like, older couple who are sort of retired, but who were crucial to Brimskarda's takeover, and so end up— You know they're, they're well looked after. But they have a useless son who cares more about history than battle. And then nobody's ever found anything to do with him at court. He's never been east, but Brimskarda'd be quite happy to send him off with you because he's useless.

Delwath: Yeah, that should be, I mean would Brimskarda, like, test to show them, you know, battle and make sure he's—you know, we would love to take him under our wing and show them what actual you know, life out on the on the eastern slopes is like, right? Like, that'd be perfect.
DM: Yeah, if you think—just don't come crying to me when he runs from the first ice worm you find. Never even seen him pick up a sword. I don't even know if he knows how to use one.
Delwath: Yeah, it's—we— We understand. We will not, we will not— we don't—we don't hold his, his honor and yours as equivalent. You're not—
DM: Oh, he doesn't have honor. Yeah, there we go, like I said, useless. Yeah, if he never came back, nobody would mind.
Riswynn: Are we just thinking big might be useful?

Delwath: No, this guy—present—these giants, I mean, what we're thinking is—what I'm thinking, at least, is these giants are all totally biased towards strength. And the one smart guy probably actually knows stuff. And he could teach us all kinds of interesting things. A giant historian of the North. Yeah, he's gonna know a ton of—a ton of stuff.

Delwath: So after the feast, I mean, we wanna meet this guy. We'll basically agree with— that we're gonna take this good for nothing with us and try and knock some sense into him. And you know, thank him for his hospitality. I don't—I think, I think we've achieved our goals here, and we should leave before we mess something up and he decides to kill us.

before: Wellby: Understanding the landscape better, and our—and the people. I mean, I know they're sort of like vermin to him. But like, what? How do we connect with them? Or how do we get closer to Ursk?
Delwath: To the— did the Vargald ever bring the giants gifts?
Wellby: Were there any of the giants who could serve as a guide to us? And how far could they do that?
Delwath: Or do any of the—yeah? Are there any of the giants who would? That's a great— Do any of the giants—is there any of the giants who want to ride on a ship for a little bit fun?
Riswynn: Or giants that have previously adventured East.
after: Wellby: Yeah.
DM: Okay. So you spend the night on the sky ship, I assume. And then the next morning find— let me just—hold on. You find Algerd, who is the Frost giant historian.
Seeker: Amazing.

DM: So, and he— I mean he was not invited. He has not met you before. He's kind of—so he's— the the sort of morning routine here, as you sort of get up in the morning, seems to be that there's always—there's always a couple of guards that you know, get up in the morning and spar. Brimskarda, apparently, like, stays up late drinking and doesn't get up in the morning.
DM: And so the sounds you hear are basically the the sparring of the giants. Then apparently, the job that this historian, Algerd, is left with is basically cleaning the goat pens.

interactions.title: Meeting Algerd at the goat pens
lines: DM: And so the sounds you hear are basically the the sparring of the giants. Then apparently, the job that this historian, Algerd, is left with is basically cleaning the goat pens.

DM: And so you find him shoveling rather large piles of goat droppings and, like, the goats are eating these like massive piles of these— of the shells of these ice gourds that the giants split open and eat the insides of which are kind of like ice cream, like sweet Italian ice kind of flavored, but the—there's like giant piles of these of the shells of these gourds scattered around this big goat pen and the goats are sort of munching away, and this giant is shoveling.

DM: It's clear that nobody's told them anything. Like, nobody's like, come and talk to him and been like "I'm sending you to—on this skyship," or anything like that. Nobody really seems to bother speaking to him at all.

Delwath: Let's like show up. And I mean, let's introduce ourselves, right? Like, start with an introduction. Right? "We are— We're travelers, we've—" And let's—I mean, why not flatter him? "We've heard, you know, a lot about the area. Or know a lot about the history of the area out right? And you know we were hoping you would talk to us for, for a bit."
DM: And he, he sort of bends down and carefully to hear you, and like, leans over. Yeah. You know, being sort of careful and polite and, and—

DM: And he's like—he doesn't— He's clean shaven. He still has a sort of slightly bluer skin which is hard to tell if it's just the light or the the way the frost giants are. His hair is relatively short, but kind of pulled back slightly and and kind of yeah, held in sort of a very short ponytail in the back. His hair itself is slightly like bluish, like dark blue. And he's wearing— He's not wearing armor. He doesn't seem to have any weapons. He's wearing like pretty dirty robes, actually.

DM: But he sort of bends down carefully and and leans in, and he and he says in a very loud sort of but slightly wavering voice like, "I heard there were little people in in here visiting. Thank you for introducing yourselves. We don't get many of your kind. Why are you talking to me?"
Delwath: We thought you might know something of value.
Delwath: The history of the East.
DM: And you would consider that of value?
Delwath: Very much. Perhaps you'd even like to see our ship. You might even know some of its history.

DM: He looks over. "I would enjoy that." Sort of stands up slightly and like, is very sort of cautious and careful around you like wants to make sure he doesn't accidentally step on any of you, and begins to sort of walk slowly and look over at the ship, looking up. It's still like 50 feet up, so just kind of peering up.
DM: "Fascinating." Bends down again very carefully to be close to you. You fly it?
Seeker: You don't—you don't have to shout. Yes, yes, some of us have the skill of ship. It is known as Vindristjarna.
DM: The Star of the wind.
DM: It must be very old.
Seeker: We think it is. Yes, it has a long history, and we are just its most recent caretakers.
DM: He kind of looks up. And again, "May I see it up close?"
Seeker: Perhaps we are protective of it, of course. We hear you're a student of history. What are you interested in?
DM: Many things. My people, your people, dragons, even sometimes the humans.
Seeker: You have any knowledge of those wizard settlements on the coast?
DM: Some. There are not many books about them.
Seeker: Books. You say you're interested in books?
DM: I am writing a book.
Seeker: And its consequences. What are its consequences? Or do I have to wait and read the book?
DM: My thesis is that Vimfrost—without Vimfrost, much would be better here.

DM: Because when he killed— they say his name was Pron— Bjarne. When he killed Bjarnfrost the Mighty, there was a power vacuum that was filled by unsavory people. Your people and my people and the shape shifters and the stoneborn all used to live in harmony.
DM: Brimskarda calls them the little people of the forest. They live in the, in the taiga. They mostly hide.
